class.name: BulletSpawner2D
class.brief_description: Fires timed volleys of bullets through a [BulletFactory2D].
class.description: Assign a [BulletFactory2D], a [BulletVolleyData2D], and a [member pattern_source]. Each volley collects one global transform per bullet from the [member transforms_generator] (empty means this node; a generator outside the tree while the spawner is inside also falls back to this node) and spawns it through the factory. It never fires in the editor. Homing quick-start: turn on [member homing_enabled], leave [member homing_target_source] on Node Group, and put your targets (any Node2D) in the [member homing_node_group] group (default "enemies"). Every volley then chases [member homing_target_selection] targets with [member homing_smoothing] turn rate. Set [member homing_target_source] to Mouse to chase the cursor instead, and turn on [member orbiting_enabled] to make bullets ring their target once they arrive. Use [member homing_retarget_mode] so flying volleys keep following fresh targets, and [signal volley_bullet_homing_target_reached] to react when a bullet arrives. Pattern quick-start: pick a [member pattern_source] helper (Ring, Fan, Spiral, Rose, Corridor...) or call [method apply_pattern_preset] for a starter, tune the matching helper_* group, and call [method shoot_once] (or enable [member shooting_enabled] for the auto loop). Add [member pattern_scale] / spin for motion, [member helper_skip_indices] for dodge doors, and [method spawn_pattern_list] for phased sequences. See [member pattern_source] for the full 33-mode list. Reparenting is safe: removing the spawner from the tree and adding it back keeps assigned nodes, tracked homing volleys, burst chains, telegraphs and pattern lists. They pause while the spawner is out of the tree and resume when it returns. Node paths are rewritten from the live nodes on re-entry, so saving the scene keeps the right targets.

method.name: adopt_live_volley
method.description: Takes ownership of a manually-woken volley (manual wake detaches the previous owner): stamps it, replaces the previous spawner's reached forwarder with its own, and tracks it for retargeting. Queues are left alone. Handlers you connected directly on the volley are kept; only spawner forwarders are replaced. Returns false for null or non-live instances.

method.name: apply_pattern_preset
method.description: Applies a named starter pattern (radial dense/sparse, 3-arm spiral, narrow/wide aimed fan, slow ring, gap wall, rain, 6-petal flower, scatter burst, cross burst, star shell, heart bloom, snake wave, waterfall curtain, petal storm via Rose, twin counter-spiral, aimed trap via Corridor, blossom finale via Rose, terrain crest via Custom) and switches pattern_source to match. Presets are clean: every Bullet Patterns knob and Spin first return to their defaults, so the same preset always gives the same pattern. The Transform subgroup (scales, muzzle offset, skip indices) and node wiring (aimed target, Path2D, custom array) are kept. Nothing fires. Custom (-1) does nothing; other values out of range fail loud. The twin counter-spiral and blossom finale presets turn spin on.

method.name: begin_burst
method.description: Starts a burst chain by hand (waves and boss phases): [member burst_count] shots, [member burst_interval_sec] apart, telegraphed first when [member telegraph_enabled]. Clears any pending telegraph first. Manual chains run whether auto-shooting is on or not; chains started by the auto loop are clamped to [method volleys_remaining] and cancelled when auto-shooting is switched off.

method.name: clear_active_bullets
method.description: Clears every live bullet this spawner owns and returns how many were cleared. With [param fire_clear_effects] (default) the On Clear effect layers fire at each bullet's pose; [code]false[/code] removes them silently. Emptied volleys return to the pool. Other spawners' bullets are untouched.

method.name: clear_live_volleys_homing
method.description: Kill-switch: clears homing queues and stops orbiting on every tracked live volley, through engine clears that keep all counters exact. Returns how many volleys were touched. Retargeting re-arms them while homing stays on; turn homing off (or clear tracking) to keep them flying straight.

method.name: collect_spawn_transforms
method.description: Returns one global transform per bullet for the current [member pattern_source]. Empty [member transforms_generator] means this node. Children mode with no markers falls back to the generator itself. Aimed mode with no target returns an empty array. Corridor mode with no target falls back to [member helper_corridor_aim_direction] so the wall still draws. Every helper pattern returns exactly [member helper_bullets_amount] transforms (gaps and fills included), minus any [member helper_skip_indices].

method.name: debug_check_layer_coincidence
method.description: Verifies every layered preview dot sits on its yellow ring (same center-scale rule and same fill deal on both sides). Returns checked/layers/max_deviation_px/mean_deviation_px/ok. Empty preview returns checked=false. Point-to-segment match: exact on sharp shapes, sub-pixel on dense sweeps.

method.name: debug_collect_spawn_transforms_uncached
method.description: Same output as [method collect_spawn_transforms], always regenerated from scratch (the bake cache is bypassed). The reference the cache-parity tests compare against.

method.name: debug_ease
method.description: Static test hook: the easing value movement uses at [param t] for a [enum Tween.TransitionType] and [enum Tween.EaseType]. Matches [method Tween.interpolate_value] for every transition and ease (pinned by tests).

method.name: debug_get_graze_preview_circles
method.description: The graze preview's rings exactly as drawn: an Array of {center, radius, color, zone_index, ring_index, target_id}. Empty while the preview is off.

method.name: debug_get_graze_preview_stats
method.description: Graze preview instrumentation: active, visible, circles, draws (how many times the layer redrew).

method.name: debug_get_layer_rings
method.description: Debug readout of the yellow preview rings: one PackedVector2Array per extra outline layer, exactly as drawn (holder-local; runs INF-separated with a closing duplicate per closed run). Empty when layers are inactive. Lets scripts and tests verify bullets sit on their rings without screenshotting the editor.

method.name: debug_get_pattern_cache_info
method.description: Bake cache introspection: [code]hits[/code], [code]misses[/code], [code]bakes[/code], [code]version[/code] (bumped by every pattern-affecting change), and [code]shot_class[/code] / [code]preview_class[/code]: -1 not baked yet, 0 regenerated every shot, 1 reused under translation only, 2 reused under any rigid motion.

method.name: debug_get_pattern_cache_verify
method.description: Whether the static cache verifier is on (see [method debug_set_pattern_cache_verify]).

method.name: debug_get_preview_dot_points
method.description: Preview bullet dots exactly as drawn (holder-local). Empty when the preview is off. Lets tests prove dots sit on the preview track.

method.name: debug_get_preview_stats
method.description: Preview instrumentation: [code]rebuilds[/code], [code]last_rebuild_usec[/code], [code]dots_draws[/code], [code]arrows_draws[/code]. Spinning or moving the spawner leaves all four flat: the pose is applied as a node transform, never as a rebuild or redraw.

method.name: debug_get_preview_track_closed
method.description: Debug/test helper: whether the drawn preview base track closes its last point back to the first.

method.name: debug_get_preview_track_points
method.description: Preview base track polyline exactly as drawn (holder-local, INF-separated runs). Empty when the preview is off. Lets tests prove the track rotates with the marker like the volley does.

method.name: debug_get_retarget_countdown
method.description: Seconds until the next interval retarget pass. Deterministically staggered per spawner so N spawners never group-scan on the same tick.

method.name: debug_set_pattern_cache_verify
method.description: Static switch for all spawners: when on, every shot or preview served from the bake cache is regenerated uncached and compared, and a mismatch pushes the error [code]BulletSpawner2D: pattern cache mismatch[/code]. Doubles generation cost: for tests only (the GUT base class turns it on for every suite).

method.name: fire_n_volleys
method.description: Arms a budget of n more volleys, then pauses. Counts every fired volley (auto or manual). [member max_volleys] is never touched, so unlimited stays unlimited. A spent budget clears itself: [method volleys_remaining] and a later [method resume_shooting] behave like an unlimited spawner again. Replaces any previous budget; unpauses a paused spawner. Rejected when n is not above zero. Works before the spawner enters the tree too (kept through _ready).

method.name: forget_tracked_volleys
method.description: Empties the retarget list (the volleys [method retarget_live_volleys] steers). The volleys themselves keep flying and keep reporting to this spawner.

method.name: get_active_live_bullet_count
method.description: Total live bullets across ALL volleys owned by this spawner (counted via the factory by ownership - plain non-homing volleys count exactly like tracked homing volleys). Budget governors and wave gates read this alongside max_live_bullets.

method.name: get_bullet_factory
method.description: Returns the factory from [member bullet_factory_path], or null when unset or invalid.

method.name: get_burst_shots_left
method.description: Shots left in the current burst chain (0 when idle). Waves and HUD can poll this to sequence phases.

method.name: get_effective_generator
method.description: Returns the node patterns are built on: the assigned generator, or this spawner when unset or invalid. Never null in the tree.

method.name: get_helper_aimed_target
method.description: Returns the shared aimed target (Aimed cone and Corridor wall), or null when unset.

method.name: get_helper_path2d_node
method.description: Returns the Path2D node used by the Path2D pattern layout, resolved from [member helper_path2d_path]. Returns null when no path is set or the node is gone. Prefer setting [member helper_path2d_path] in the inspector; this accessor is for runtime lookups.

method.name: get_live_volley_count
method.description: How many live volleys this spawner owns (factory census).

method.name: get_live_volleys
method.description: Every live volley this spawner owns (a census of the factory, not capped by the retarget list), so scripts can call the full [BulletVolley2D] API on each. Handles can go stale: a volley whose last bullet died returns to the pool and may serve another owner, so compare [method BulletVolley2D.get_life_id] or check [method BulletVolley2D.is_pooled] before steering a volley you held across frames.

method.name: get_movement_leg
method.description: Legs completed since the run started. A leg is one traversal of the path; Ping Pong counts each direction as a leg.

method.name: get_movement_path_node
method.description: The resolved [Path2D] behind [member movement_path], or null when unset, freed or outside the tree.

method.name: get_movement_progress
method.description: Distance ratio along the path: 0 = path start, 1 = path end, independent of the leg direction.

method.name: get_movement_velocity
method.description: Velocity of the last movement step in px/s; zero while paused, stopped, waiting (start delay, endpoint pause) or not moving. This is the velocity [member inherit_movement_velocity] adds to bullets.

method.name: get_setup_warnings
method.description: The same list as the editor's configuration warning icon: no factory, factory path not pointing to a [BulletFactory2D], no spawn data or invisible spawn data, Aimed/Corridor without a target, Path2D pattern without a path, empty Custom pattern, movement on without a path, orbiting without homing. Empty when nothing is misconfigured. Callable from scripts for debug UIs and CI scene checks.

method.name: get_spin_angle_deg
method.description: Current spin angle in degrees. Only advances at runtime while [member spin_enabled] is on.

method.name: get_tracked_volley_count
method.description: How many volleys are on the retarget list (homing volleys this spawner fired, capped at 256; the oldest drops first).

method.name: get_transforms_generator
method.description: Returns the assigned generator, or null when unset. Use [method get_effective_generator] when you need the fallback included.

method.name: get_volleys_fired
method.description: Volleys fired since the last (re)arm. Reset with [method reset_shooting].

method.name: is_movement_playing
method.description: True while the run is playing, including its start delay and endpoint pauses; false when paused, stopped or finished.

method.name: is_pattern_list_active
method.description: Whether a pattern list is currently queued/firing.

method.name: is_shooting_active
method.description: Effective shooting state: switch on, not paused, cap not reached. This is configured state (true outside the tree too), not whether a tick is imminent.

method.name: is_shooting_paused
method.description: Whether [method pause_shooting] is latched. While set, no volley is created (burst, telegraph, pattern-list and timer chains freeze); spin, retargeting and preview keep running.

method.name: movement_pause
method.description: Freezes the movement in place, keeping progress, leg and timers; [method movement_play] resumes from there.

method.name: movement_play
method.description: Starts the movement, or resumes it after [method movement_pause]. A finished or stopped run restarts from the beginning ([member movement_start_ratio] and [member movement_start_delay_sec] apply again). Emits [signal movement_started] when it was not already playing. Runtime only: ignored in the editor.

method.name: movement_reverse
method.description: Flips the current leg's direction in place: the spawner turns around where it is and the eased progress continues smoothly the other way.

method.name: movement_seek
method.description: Jumps to [param ratio] (0..1) of the current leg, measured along the leg's direction, and moves the spawner there. A NaN or out-of-range ratio fails loud and is ignored.

method.name: movement_stop
method.description: Stops the movement. With [param reset_to_start] (default) the run resets and the spawner snaps back to the start pose; otherwise it stays where it is and the run counts as finished. [method movement_play] restarts from the beginning either way. Emits no signal.

method.name: override_live_volleys_velocity
method.description: Overwrites velocity on every tracked live volley (wind, knockback). A speed curve overrides direct velocity, so this visibly works only for curve-free volleys. Returns how many volleys were touched. Must be finite.

method.name: pause_shooting
method.description: Freezes volley creation keeping all counters: burst, telegraph, pattern-list and timer chains hold where they are and resume on [method resume_shooting]. Spin, retargeting and preview are unaffected. Manual [method shoot_once] still fires. Emits [signal shooting_stopped] on the active-to-idle transition (inside the tree only; a pause made before the tree is kept through _ready).

method.name: reset_shooting
method.description: Resets the volley counter, clears pause and any [method fire_n_volleys] budget, clears burst/telegraph chains and the pattern-list queue, re-arms the timer with [member shoot_initial_delay_sec] and the retarget clock, and emits [signal shooting_started] when auto-shooting resumes (inside the tree only).

method.name: reset_spin_angle
method.description: Resets the spin angle to zero.

method.name: resolve_graze_targets
method.description: The [Node2D] targets the runtime would test for [member graze_zones] entry [param zone_index] right now: the first 4 live members of its target group in tree order, this spawner excluded. Empty for an empty slot or a disabled zone; an out-of-range index pushes an error.

method.name: resolve_homing_targets
method.description: Resolves the current homing targets without touching any volley: group members, name matches (case-insensitive unless [member homing_node_name_case_sensitive]), children of the parent path, the node at [member homing_target_path], or the [member homing_global_position] snapshot. The Mouse source returns an empty array (the cursor is pushed live, not resolved). Entries are Node2D or Vector2. Unless quiet is true, an empty result warns once per homing configuration (shots share the same warning). With advance_round_robin off, the round-robin pick is resolved without consuming the cursor (retarget passes use this so flying volleys keep stable targets).

method.name: resume_shooting
method.description: Clears [method pause_shooting]: frozen chains continue where they held. Emits [signal shooting_started] on the idle-to-active transition (inside the tree only).

method.name: retarget_live_volleys
method.description: Re-resolves targets and replaces the queues of every still-active volley owned by this spawner (expired or pooled volleys are skipped), and re-applies steering and orbiting tuning so runtime changes reach flying volleys. Random and round-robin selections resolve per volley. Volleys with no resolvable targets are skipped quietly and keep their old queues. Volleys whose bullets are all disabled are skipped too: the tick never moves disabled slots, so pushing targets there would only inflate counters. Returns how many volleys were retargeted. Also runs automatically when [member homing_retarget_mode] is On Interval. Only the newest volley is touched when [member homing_retarget_previous_volleys] is off. Locked orbit rings survive the replace per the lock policy ([member orbiting_lock_policy]) instead of always re-locking.

method.name: set_bullet_factory
method.description: Assigns the factory directly. Pass null to clear it.

method.name: set_helper_aimed_target
method.description: Assigns the shared aimed target (Aimed cone and Corridor wall) directly. Pass null to clear it.

method.name: set_helper_path2d_node
method.description: Assigns the Path2D node used by the Path2D pattern layout. Updates [member helper_path2d_path] to point at it and refreshes the editor preview. Pass null to clear it.

method.name: set_movement_path_node
method.description: Assigns the [Path2D] to move along and stores its path in [member movement_path].

method.name: set_transforms_generator
method.description: Assigns the generator directly. Pass null to use this spawner instead. Takes effect right away, in the editor and at runtime.

method.name: shoot_once
method.description: Fires one volley now. Returns false when misconfigured or the factory refuses it. Counts toward [member max_volleys] and any [method fire_n_volleys] budget. Safe to call from _physics_process (same-shape pool reuse applies immediately; only a shape-type change waits for a safe point). Must not be called re-entrantly from inside spawner signal handlers (pre_shoot, homing_targets_resolved, volley_homing_configured, volley_fired, volley_skipped, shooting_finished): nested calls are rejected, use [method shoot_once_deferred] (or call_deferred("shoot_once")) instead. This also means intentional synchronous cascades (a handler firing another spawner immediately) are deferred by one frame by design. If a handler frees or re-homes the volley mid-setup (including pre_shoot, which is validated before configuring), the shot is safely dropped (returns false) instead of emitting volley_fired with a dead instance.

method.name: shoot_once_deferred
method.description: Queues a [method shoot_once] with call_deferred so it runs after the current emission / physics step instead of nesting. Use this from spawner signal handlers or colliding contexts. Returns true once queued (the shot itself reports through volley_fired or volley_skipped); false when the spawner is not inside the tree.

method.name: spawn_pattern_list
method.description: Fires pattern entries: each entry is a Dictionary with optional "preset", "pattern_source", "helper_bullets_amount" and "spawn_data" keys. Every entry is a temporary override: after it fires, the spawner returns to its own configuration (including anything a preset entry changed). Sequential mode (default) fires one entry per interval_sec; simultaneous mode fires all at once. Returns entries queued (sequential) or volleys fired (simultaneous). Bad entries and unknown keys fail loud and are skipped, never aborting the list. Both modes emit [signal pattern_list_finished] once at the end.

method.name: stop_pattern_list
method.description: Cancels the active pattern list (queued entries are dropped, fired volleys keep flying).

method.name: volleys_remaining
method.description: Volleys left before [member max_volleys] trips or the [method fire_n_volleys] budget runs out, whichever is smaller. -1 means unlimited (no cap and no budget left).

members.member: Path to the [BulletFactory2D] used for spawning. Inside the tree, a path to a node of another type is rejected (old value kept).
Mirror every other burst volley (fan/spiral chirality flip). The first shot is plain, then shots alternate, for any burst_count.
Shots per burst trigger. Must be between 1 and 1024. Shrinking it during a chain ends the chain at the new count.
Fire multi-volley bursts per trigger: each interval pulls the trigger for burst_count shots spaced burst_interval_sec apart. Mid-burst shots ignore the main interval.
Seconds between burst shots. Must be finite and above zero.
Master switch: every volley this spawner fires is armed with [member graze_zones]. Changes apply to the next shots; volleys already flying keep their zones.
Also draw the graze rings while the game runs (debugging aid). Requires [member graze_show_preview].
Line width of the graze preview rings, in pixels. Must be finite and above zero.

Draw every ring of every zone around each resolved target in the zone's [member BulletGrazeZone2D.preview_color]: in the editor, and at runtime only with [member graze_preview_during_runtime]. The rings follow moving targets without rebuilding anything else.

Up to 4 [BulletGrazeZone2D] zones armed on every fired volley; null entries are kept and skipped. A shared [code].tres[/code] works across spawners. Assign the whole array: one changed in place still arms its first 4 zones but warns once.
Center the cone on the target. Off starts it to one side.

Blend toward the predicted target position: 0 aims at where the target is now, 1 fully leads it by helper_aimed_prediction_time at its current velocity (needs get_velocity on the target, else aims live).
Seconds of travel to lead the target by at full helper_aimed_prediction.
Aimed cone width in radians.
Spacing between aimed origins so bullets do not stack.
Node the aimed cone points at (also steers the Corridor wall when one is assigned). No target means no bullets in Aimed mode; Corridor falls back to helper_corridor_aim_direction.

Bullet count for helper patterns: every generated pattern draws exactly this many bullets, each on its own spot (Fill Inside, Corridor and Ellipse Wall included). Clamped to 1-10000: one volley fans out to transforms, instance buffers and physics shapes, so uncapped values would freeze on a typo. Children, Self and Custom take their count from the markers or the array instead.
Circle bullets face outward (away from the generator); off faces inward (toward it).
Extra facing twist in degrees on top of the circle normal. Must be finite.
Exact circle loop radius in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Fallback aim axis (need not be normalized). The live aimed target wins when one is assigned. Must be finite and non-zero.
Face every slot down the aim axis. Off faces each slot away from the marker instead.
Extra facing twist in degrees. Must be finite.

Center dodge door in pixels. All [member helper_bullets_amount] bullets are split over the two wall segments, and the door stays empty. Must be finite and 0 or more. Width and gap are independent (scene load order never matters); a door as wide as the wall is drawn at half the width, with one warning.
Wall width in pixels across the aim axis. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Angle growth per step along each arm in radians (odd arms wind the opposite way when mirrored). Must be finite.
Below the arm count, consecutive slots interleave across arms; from the arm count up, each arm takes runs of consecutive slots. Every slot always lands on its own (arm, step) spot. Must be 1 or more.
Counter-rotating arms. Must be 2 or more (use Multi Spiral for 1 arm).
Per-arm facing: tangent (travel direction), radial outward, toward center, or keep marker.
Twists every arm facing. Must be finite.
Mirror every other arm so neighbours counter-rotate (galaxy/windmill). Off winds all arms the same way like Multi Spiral.
Radius growth per step along each arm. Must be finite.
Rotate the arm phases with the marker. Off aims arms in global space.
First-slot radius in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Rays in the cross/plus barrage. Must be 1 or more.
How far each ray reaches from the marker. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Base rotation of the cross in radians.
Whether slots face away from the marker along their ray.
Extra facing twist in degrees.

Spacing between slots along each ray. When an arm cannot hold its share of bullets at this spacing, the spacing shrinks so the outermost slot sits on the arm tip (every bullet keeps its own spot). Must be finite and above zero.

Which direction Custom bullets face: As Stored keeps each transform's rotation, Face Outward/Inward aims radially from the generator, +90/-90 Degrees turn the stored rotation across it. helper_custom_facing_offset_deg still applies on top.
Extra facing twist in degrees on top of the Custom facing. Must be finite.
Mirrors the Custom array order: bullet 0 moves to the far end.
Rotates which Custom array slot becomes bullet 0 (wraps both ways).

Hand-placed volley in generator-local pixels: each stored transform spawns exactly one bullet there (composed as marker * local, so spin and scales keep working). Empty by default (Custom draws nothing until you fill it). Every entry must be finite. The count comes from the array itself; helper_bullets_amount is ignored. Apply TERRAIN_CREST once for a starter crest line.
Diamond horizontal diagonal in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Diamond vertical diagonal in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Diamond bullets face outward; off faces inward.
Extra facing twist in degrees on top of the diamond normal. Must be finite.
Diamond base rotation in radians. Must be finite.
Arc span for Arc and Wall modes. A full turn (or within half a slot of one) closes the ring like Full mode. Must be finite.
Face along the ellipse outward normal. Off faces inward.
Twists every ellipse facing. Must be finite.
Dodge gaps in Wall mode. Shown only in Wall mode. Must be between 0 and 10000.
Width of each Wall gap in radians. Shown only in Wall mode. Must be finite and 0 or more.

0 draws the full ring, 1 draws an arc segment, 2 draws a wall with dodge gaps: all [member helper_bullets_amount] bullets are shared by the solid stretches and the gaps stay empty. Wall mode with gap_count 0 or gap_width 0 draws the plain arc. An Arc or Wall spanning a full turn closes like the full ring (no doubled seam bullet).
Ellipse semi-axis X in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Ellipse semi-axis Y in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Rotates the ellipse axes. Must be finite.
Where Arc/Wall segments start. Must be finite.
Per-slot random angle variance in radians for shotgun spreads. 0 fires the exact cone. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Center the fan on its direction. Off starts it to one side.
Fan center direction in radians.
Seed for fan angle jitter only. 0 is non-deterministic, otherwise every volley lands identically. Does nothing while [member helper_fan_angle_jitter] is 0. Only shown for the Fan pattern.
Fan width in radians.
Spacing between fan origins so bullets do not stack.
Rotates the whole flower. Must be finite.
Face away from the marker. Off faces the marker (implosion blossoms).
Twists every flower facing. Must be finite.
Core-hole lift for RHODONEA, PHYLLOTAXIS, SUPERFORMULA: 0 is a full bloom, closer to 1 lifts the waist into a ring. Must be finite in [0, 1).
Pinch between lobes: 0 is round, higher is tighter. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Angular width of each FAN lobe in radians. When the lobes touch or overlap, edge slots of neighboring petals never land on the same spot. Must be finite and 0 or more.

Lobes in the flower pattern. In FAN mode the [member helper_bullets_amount] bullets are split evenly over the petals (the remainder spread symmetrically; fewer bullets than petals light evenly spaced petals). Must be 1 or more.
Flower radius in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
SPIROGRAPH only: hypotrochoid pen offset d (>= 0). Larger values stretch the loops outward.
SPIROGRAPH only: hypotrochoid roller radius r (> 0). Larger values pull the lacy loops tighter.
SUPERFORMULA only: fullness exponent controlling round vs. pinched petal shape. Must be finite in (0, 8].
SUPERFORMULA only: lobe count m of the simplified Gielis curve. Must be finite in [2, 64].
Bloom kind selector (0 FAN, 1 RHODONEA, 2 PHYLLOTAXIS, 3 SPIROGRAPH, 4 SUPERFORMULA). Per-type knobs below apply only to their matching bloom kind.
Grid anchor, same values as [constant BulletFactory2D.CENTER] (0 TOP_LEFT through 8 BOTTOM_RIGHT).
Grid horizontal spacing.
Random position offset per grid bullet. 0 is off.
Give each grid bullet a random facing.
Rotate the grid with the generator.
Grid vertical spacing.
Grid rows per column.

Seed for grid jitter and random rotation only. 0 is non-deterministic, otherwise every volley lands identically. Does nothing while [member helper_grid_jitter] is 0 and random rotation is off. Only shown for the Grid pattern.
Base rotation of the heart in radians.
Whether slots face away from the heart center.
Extra facing twist in degrees.
Heart outline size in pixels. Must be finite and above zero.
Honeycomb columns. Must be between 1 and 40000 (columns times rows is capped at 40000 at generation, with one warning).
Whether slots face away from the marker.
Extra facing twist in degrees.
Honeycomb rows. Must be 1 or more.
Horizontal spacing in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Vertical spacing in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Offset odd rows by half spacing for the honeycomb look.
Where the generator sits on the line, same values as [constant BulletFactory2D.LINE_ANCHOR_CENTER] (0 START, 1 CENTER, 2 END).
Line axis. Does not need to be normalized.
Face line bullets along the line. Off keeps the generator facing.

Which direction line bullets face: along the line (as generated: axis or marker per helper_line_face_direction), or turned +90/-90 degrees across it. The per-line facing_offset_deg still applies on top. Replaces the old perpendicular toggle.
Mirrors the line row order: bullet 0 moves to the far end.
Rotates which line slot becomes bullet 0 (wraps both ways).
Distance between line bullets. Must be finite and above zero (helper_line_reverse flips the order).
Shifts the whole line row along its axis in pixels, on top of the Start/Center/End anchor. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Face away from the curve center. Off faces inward.
Extra facing twist in degrees. Must be finite.

Horizontal weave frequency. Ratios sharing a factor (3:3) are drawn once, and curves that fold back on themselves (1:1 at phase 0) are spread along the open run, so every bullet stays visible. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Vertical weave frequency. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Phase offset in radians (morphs the figure-8 into its weave variants). Must be finite.
Weave half-width in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Weave half-height in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Angle growth per step along each arm. Must be finite.
Below the arm count, consecutive slots interleave across arms; from the arm count up, each arm takes runs of consecutive slots. Every slot always lands on its own (arm, step) spot. Must be 1 or more.
Interleaved spiral arms. Must be 1 or more.
Per-arm facing: tangent (travel direction), radial outward, toward center, or keep marker.
Twists every arm facing. Must be finite.
Radius growth per step along each arm. Must be finite.
Rotate the arm phases with the marker. Off aims arms in global space.
First-slot radius in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.

Which normal a corner-seated dot uses on corner-anchored shapes: Side (owning side's edge normal, stable default), Miter (angle bisector: triangle apexes face UP), Smooth (averaged loop normals everywhere: coherent on spiky stars). Corner shapes only.

Pin Corners seats a dot on every corner (interiors spread per edge); Even Arc spreads purely evenly by arc length from corner 0 (corners coincide only when the count aligns; best for dense volleys). Corner shapes only.

Which adjoining side owns a shared corner dot on corner-anchored shapes (Rectangle, Square, Polygon, Triangle, Trapezoid, Diamond, Star): Horizontal Sides (top/bottom own corners, so a top-right dot faces UP), Vertical Sides (left/right own them), Balanced (outgoing edge owns, previous behavior). On-outline and layers layouts only.

How corner-anchored polygon loops (Rectangle, Square, Polygon, Triangle, Trapezoid, Diamond, Star) spread leftover slots: Legacy fills the first edges in winding order (equal sides can differ), Symmetric pairs opposite edges so opposite sides stay equal. Smooth loops (Circle, Ellipse and the non-polygon generators) resample evenly regardless, so this knob is hidden there — it is a dead setting on those shapes, not a missing feature.
Interior dots keep at least this many pixels of clearance from corners along their edge (clamped per edge; corners stay pinned). Only shown in Pin Corners mode. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Rotates each closed-loop shape facing: Outline Normal keeps it as generated, +90/-90 Degrees turn it toward the loop tangent. The per-shape facing_offset_deg still applies on top.
Keep-out distance in pixels from the loop edge for Fill Inside cells. Must be finite and 0 or more.

Interior grid cell size in pixels for Fill Inside. Used as-is whenever every bullet fits; when they do not, the spacing shrinks just enough. When more cells fit than bullets, the bullets are picked evenly over the whole shape. Must be finite and above zero.
Shifts every other Fill Inside row by half a cell (honeycomb packing).
How many concentric rings share the volley in Layers placement. 1 is a single exact layer (the default, identical to On Outline). Must be in [1, 64].

How bullets are dealt across layers: Interleaved (bullet i rides layer i % count, winding survives), Sequential (fills contiguous chunks starting from [member helper_outline_layer_start_offset], so small volleys still read as the base shape with offset 0), Outer First (sequential from the outermost ring inward) or Ping Pong (waves 0..last..0, pairs with spin). Layers placement only.

How Layers placement assigns polygon bullets to rings: Shared Loop decimates one loop (outer rings miss corners), Even Per Layer rebuilds an even symmetric loop per ring (corners on every ring). Layers placement only.

Max bullets kept per extra layer (0 = unlimited): overflow is dropped, first-kept in bullet order, so the volley may shrink below helper_bullets_amount. Layer 0 is never capped. Layers placement only.
Fractional growth per layer: each extra ring rescales the shape about the loop center (0.2 = 20% bigger per layer outward). Must be finite in (0, 8]. Layers placement only.
Ring-size progression: Linear steps evenly, Exponential compounds ((1 + step)^L, mirrored reciprocally inward). A non-empty [member helper_outline_layer_scales] overrides both. Layers placement only.

Explicit per-layer scales, entry L % size (e.g. [1.0, 1.5, 1.6] for a tight outer pair). Empty means the formula above. Each entry must be finite in [0.05, 64], at most 64 entries. Layers placement only.
Which side of the base outline extra layers grow toward: Outward (each ring bigger), Inward (rings crowd toward the center), or Both (alternating bigger/smaller). Layers placement only.

Which layer Sequential-family filling starts from (wraps around, so 1 starts on the second ring and the outline fills last). 0 starts on the outline. Only shown — and only consumed — in Layers placement with Sequential or Outer First fill; Interleaved and Ping Pong ignore it. Must be 0 or more.
Slot rotation per successive layered ring (0 = off, negatives wrap): stacked rings interleave angularly instead of sitting in spokes. Layer 0 is never twisted. Layers placement only.

Where closed-loop shape bullets live (Ring, Ellipse, Star, Flower, Rose, Lissajous, Circle, Rectangle, Square, Polygon, Triangle, Trapezoid, Diamond, Heart): On Outline keeps the generated slot loop exactly (single layer, the default), Layers re-spawns the same figure scaled about the loop center (each ring sampled from the true curve), Fill Inside fills the shape's interior with exactly [member helper_bullets_amount] grid cells.
Mirrors the closed-loop slot order (winding flip): bullet 0 moves to the far end of the loop. On-outline and layers layouts only.
Rotates which closed-loop slot becomes bullet 0 (wraps both ways). On-outline and layers layouts only.
Where a fixed Path2D run sits when shorter than the curve: Path Start, Centered, or Path End (Fixed Spacing mode only). helper_path2d_start_offset shifts on top of this.

Treat the Path2D curve as a loop: the last-to-first stretch is measured so spacing wraps. A curve already drawn as a loop (last point on the first) becomes a clean ring with no doubled seam bullet; two-point outlines always stay open.

How Path2D bullets are placed: Fixed Spacing lays helper_bullets_amount bullets helper_path2d_spacing apart (helper_path2d_anchor/overflow decide placement when the run is shorter/longer than the curve), Spread Evenly covers the whole curve length (both endpoints included on open paths; seamless ring without a duplicated seam bullet on closed loops).
Which direction Path2D bullets face: Along Path (+X with travel, the tangent), Normal +90, or Normal -90. helper_path2d_facing_offset_deg applies on top.
Extra facing twist in degrees on top of the Path2D facing. Must be finite.

What happens when a fixed Path2D run does not fit (run longer than the curve, or shifted past its ends): Clamp stacks the extras on the curve end (an explicit choice), Wrap continues from the start, Auto Fit scales spacing down so the run fits exactly (Fixed Spacing mode only; a closed loop spreads over its full length with no seam duplicate).

Path2D node to live-sample bullet positions from (baked curve points, re-resolved every volley, ObjectDB-guarded, expressed in the generator space). Bullets sit exactly on the curve per helper_path2d_distribution; empty means no outline.
Walk the Path2D curve end to start (exact mirror: bullet 0 lands on the curve end). Along Path facing flips with it.

Which frame the Path2D curve is drawn in. Follow Generator (default) copies the curve shape onto the generator with its bounding-box center reset to the origin: only the shape matters, the node's own transform and wherever the curve was drawn are ignored (moving/rotating the Path2D node does nothing), like every other pattern. At Path2D Node keeps the legacy pose: the volley materializes where the node sits in the world. Flip back to this if an existing scene relied on the old default. When the path is a child of the generator at origin, both modes coincide.
Offset in pixels between consecutive Path2D bullets (Fixed Spacing mode only). Must be finite and greater than 0.

Distance in pixels along the Path2D curve where layout starts (Fixed: first-bullet position on top of the anchor; Spread Evenly: phase-rotates a loop, or pushes an open run toward the end, clamped). Must be finite and 0 or more.
Polygon bullets face outward; off faces inward.
Extra facing twist in degrees on top of the polygon normal. Must be finite.
Polygon corner radius in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Polygon base rotation in radians. Must be finite.
Polygon corner count (true perimeter, not the Star Polygon scatter mode). Must be between 3 and 10000.
Width of the rain band in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Direction the rain falls (need not be normalized). Must be finite and non-zero.
Row spacing of the layered sheets. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Random offset per slot in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Seed for rain jitter only. 0 is non-deterministic, otherwise every volley lands identically. Does nothing while [member helper_rain_jitter] is 0. Only shown for the Rain pattern.
Rectangle bullets face outward; off faces inward.
Extra facing twist in degrees on top of the rectangle normal. Must be finite.
Rectangle perimeter size in pixels, centered on the generator. Must be finite with sides 0 or more.
Ring length in radians. Full circle by default; a full turn (or within half a slot of one) closes the ring without a doubled seam bullet.
Face bullets away from the center. Off faces them inward.
Twists every ring facing by this many degrees.
Ring radius around the generator.
Give each ring bullet a random facing.
Rotate the ring with the generator.
Seed for ring random rotation only. 0 is non-deterministic, otherwise every volley lands identically. Does nothing while [member helper_ring_random_rotation] is off. Only shown for the Ring pattern.
Angle in radians where the ring starts.
Squashes the ring into an ellipse. 1.0 is a circle. Must be finite and above zero.
Rotates the whole rose in radians. Must be finite.
Face along the petal axis away from the center. Off faces inward.
Extra facing twist in degrees. Must be finite.
Lobe pinch: 1.0 is the exact rose, 0 is round, higher is tighter. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Rose lobes (rhodonea k): odd values draw k petals, even values 2k petals, each traced once (no stacked bullets). Must be 2 or more.
Rose radius in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Sector width in radians around [member helper_scatter_direction]. TAU or more is a full circle; narrow it (with a direction) for cones of fire. Must be finite and above 0.
Outer radius of the burst disc in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more. Use it for explosions, boss deaths and pops: wide radius with many bullets reads as a blast, small radius as a pop.
Center of the scatter sector. Only matters when [member helper_scatter_arc] is below TAU. Must be finite and non-zero. Use it for directional blasts and shotgun fans.
Bullet facing: 0 outward (explosions), 1 random (shotgun spray), 2 inward (implosions).

Random twist on each outward/inward facing in radians (ignored by random facing, which is already random). Must be finite and 0 or more. Small values keep the radial look, large values dissolve it into spray.

Inner radius of the burst annulus in pixels. 0 is a full disc; above 0 the center stays empty for explosion rings. Clamped to [member helper_scatter_burst_radius] at generation, so set order never matters.

Scatter-only seed: 0 is non-deterministic, otherwise every volley lands identically (combine with spin for rotating replays). Drives burst positions, sector angles and random facings of this pattern only.

Slot indexes to drop from any helper layout (dodge doors, bullet text). Out-of-range entries are ignored with one warning per pattern change (never from the preview). Applied after spin/scale so indexes match the preview.
Angle step in radians per spiral bullet.
Spiral facing, same values as [constant BulletFactory2D.SPIRAL_FACING_TANGENT] (0 TANGENT, 1 RADIAL_OUTWARD, 2 TOWARD_CENTER, 3 KEEP_MARKER).
Twists every spiral facing by this many degrees.
Radius growth per spiral bullet.
Rotate the spiral with the generator.
Radius of the first spiral bullet.
Square bullets face outward; off faces inward.
Extra facing twist in degrees on top of the square normal. Must be finite.
Square perimeter side length in pixels, centered on the generator. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Base rotation of the star in radians.
Whether slots face away from the marker.
Extra facing twist in degrees.
Inner vertex radius. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Outer vertex radius. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Star points (alternating outer/inner vertices). Must be between 2 and 10000.
Rotates the whole star. Must be finite.
Face away from the marker. Off faces the marker.
Twists every star facing. Must be finite.
Star radius in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Star sharpness: 0 is an even ring, higher pulls density toward the vertices. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Star vertices. Must be 3 or more.
Trapezoid bottom base width in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Trapezoid top base width in pixels (0 degrades to a triangle). Must be finite and 0 or more.
Trapezoid bullets face outward; off faces inward.
Extra facing twist in degrees on top of the trapezoid normal. Must be finite.
Trapezoid height in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Trapezoid base rotation in radians. Must be finite.
Triangle bullets face outward; off faces inward.
Extra facing twist in degrees on top of the triangle normal. Must be finite.
Triangle base rotation in radians. Must be finite.
Equilateral circumradius / isosceles base width / right X leg in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Isosceles height / right Y leg in pixels (unused by Equilateral). Must be finite and 0 or more.

Triangle kind: Equilateral (circumradius helper_triangle_size_a), Isosceles (base helper_triangle_size_a + height helper_triangle_size_b, apex up), Right (legs helper_triangle_size_a along X and helper_triangle_size_b along Y, recentered). All centered on the generator.
Horizontal spacing in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Curtain columns. Must be between 1 and 40000 (columns times rows is capped at 40000 at generation, with one warning).
Extra facing twist in degrees. Must be finite.
Random offset per slot in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Fall direction (need not be normalized). Must be finite and non-zero.
Row spacing in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Curtain rows. Must be 1 or more.
Seed for waterfall jitter only. 0 is non-deterministic, otherwise every volley lands identically. Does nothing while [member helper_waterfall_jitter] is 0. Only shown for the Waterfall pattern.
Per-row stagger factor. Must be finite.
Sine amplitude in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Row axis (need not be normalized). Must be finite and non-zero.
Whether slots face along the wave tangent.
Extra facing twist in degrees.
Wave count across the row. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Snake row width in pixels. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Advances the homing queue when a target is reached: per bullet in Per Bullet mode, once for the shared queue in Shared mode.

Parent whose Node2D children are chased for the Node Children source (the whole subtree with [member homing_children_recursive], walking through non-Node2D nodes). Required: an empty or invalid path fires plain volleys and warns once. The spawner itself is never chased.
Includes grandchildren and deeper descendants for the Node Children source.
Seconds of straight flight before volley steering starts (classic aimed-then-homing). 0 steers immediately. Must be finite and 0 or more.
A target counts as reached inside this distance. Predictive, so fast bullets still trigger.
Seconds of steering before volleys fly straight (lets fast players escape). 0 is infinite. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Master switch: every volley chases the configured targets. Off means volleys fly exactly as the spawn data says.
Extra allow-list on top of any source: only targets also in this group are kept. Empty means no filtering.

Fire cone in degrees around the spawner facing including spin (homing only): a volley with resolved targets but none inside half this angle is skipped before spawning (volley_skipped "outside_fire_arc"). A passing volley chases exactly the targets the cone approved (one resolution per shot). Empty resolutions still fire plain volleys; the mouse source never resolves, so the cone ignores it. 0 is omnidirectional. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Position chased per volley for the Global Position source. Must be finite.
Volley steering pauses while the bullet is farther than this from its target. 0 is unlimited. Must be finite and 0 or more.

Detection radius around the effective generator (the volley's muzzle: [member transforms_generator_path] when set, else the spawner) for the node group, node name, and node children sources. Nearest selection measures from the same point. 0 is unlimited.

How many targets enter the queue. 1 is classic single-target homing. Only the node group, node name, and node children sources use it. Valid range is 1-10000; each homing queue caps at 256 entries, so larger resolutions are clamped to 256 per queue.
0 shares one target queue across the whole volley, 1 gives every bullet its own queue (same targets each).
Polled group for the Node Group source. Only Node2D members can be chased; other members, the spawner itself and nodes queued for deletion are skipped.

Name pattern chased for the Node Name source. The whole scene is scanned, so dynamically spawned enemies are found with no group setup. The spawner itself and its child markers never match, and [BulletFactory2D] subtrees (volleys, attachments, effects) are never scanned. Prefer the Node Group source in large scenes: the scan visits every node once per volley.
Compares node names strictly. Off (default) matches "Player" against "PlAyEr".
How the node name source compares names: exact, contains, starts with, or ends with.
Fans smoothing out per bullet: bullet i steers with start + step times i.

Seed for homing random-target selection ([constant BulletSpawner2D.HOMING_SELECT_RANDOM]) only. 0 is non-deterministic, otherwise picks reproduce. Only shown when that selection is active. Does not affect steering, smoothing, retargeting or any bullet pattern.
Seconds between automatic retarget passes. Must be above zero.
0 leaves flying volleys alone, On Interval re-resolves and replaces their queues every interval. On by default so group, name, and children tracking stays live as members spawn and die.

Explicit time to the first retarget pass. 0 (default) staggers it per spawner automatically, so many spawners never scene-scan on the same tick. The period stays homing_retarget_interval_sec. Must be finite and 0 or more.
Retargeting re-aims every tracked live volley. Turn off to re-aim only the newest volley, letting older ones fly at whatever they chased last.

Max turn rate in radians per second. 0 snaps instantly. A bullet cannot turn tighter than speed / smoothing pixels, so to be sure it hits, keep that radius smaller than the target's hitbox (raise the smoothing for fast bullets or small targets).
Per-bullet smoothing of the first bullet.
Per-bullet smoothing growth per bullet. May be negative, results clamp at 0.
Lets homing steer the bullet facing. Turn off only when a movement pattern, rotation data, or orbiting texture mode already owns the facing, otherwise homing steers nothing.

Node chased per volley for the Node Path source. Must point at a live Node2D in the tree: a freed, removed or dying target means the volley flies without homing (warned once). Inside the tree, a path to a non-Node2D is rejected and the old value kept; an unresolved path is accepted (the node may be added later).
Which detected nodes become targets: nearest to the spawner, random, tree order, round robin across volleys, or dealt across bullets (Per Bullet mode only).

Where volley targets come from: a node group, the mouse cursor, a global position snapshot, a node path, a node name, or a node's children. Each source shows its own settings, like the pattern_source helper patterns do. Sources never pick the spawner itself, its pattern markers, nodes under a [BulletFactory2D], nodes already queued for deletion, or non-Node2D nodes. When a shot finds no target it still fires as a plain volley, and a warning explaining why prints once per homing configuration (changing any homing target setting re-arms it).
Seconds between target position refreshes. 0 refreshes every tick.

Bullets fired while the spawner moves inherit its movement velocity ([method get_movement_velocity] x [member movement_velocity_inherit_factor]), so a moving turret's shots carry its momentum for their whole life. Homing bullets aim through that momentum (they cancel it across the line of sight), but only while their own speed is larger than the sideways part of the inherited velocity: lower the factor for slow homing bullets. Off by default.

Soft live-bullet fuse: 0 is unlimited, otherwise a shot is skipped (volley_skipped "over_budget") while this spawner's live bullets (homing and plain volleys, counted via the factory) reach this count. The check runs before any pattern work, so a stalled spawner costs nothing. Retargeting is not affected. The census is O(factory volleys) per trigger pull: fine for a handful of budgeted spawners.

Auto-shooting stops after this many volleys. -1 is infinite, 0 disables auto-shooting ([method shoot_once] still works). Lowering the cap below the fired count emits [signal shooting_stopped] (raising it back emits [signal shooting_started]); [signal shooting_finished] fires once from the volley that trips the cap, so a volley_fired handler that lowers the cap never double-fires it. Untouched by [method fire_n_volleys].
Start moving automatically on ready, and when [member movement_enabled] is switched on at runtime. Off: call [method movement_play] yourself.
Sample the path with cubic interpolation (the [code]cubic[/code] argument of [method Curve2D.sample_baked]) for smoother motion on coarse bakes. Off: linear between baked points (cheaper).
Direction of the first leg: Forward (path start to end) or Reverse (end to start).
Seconds per leg when [member movement_timing] is Duration. Must be finite and greater than 0.
[enum Tween.EaseType] applied to each leg's progress (In, Out, In Out, Out In), exactly like a Tween. Hidden when [member movement_progress_curve] is set.

Master switch: the spawner node travels along [member movement_path] at runtime (never in the editor). Movement runs before shooting and the preview each frame, so shots and the gizmo use the updated pose. Every pattern keeps working while moving; patterns that follow the spawner stay baked (no regeneration per shot).
Dwell time at each endpoint between legs (Loop and Ping Pong). Not applied after the final leg.
Once: one leg, then [signal movement_finished]. Loop: every leg starts again from the path start (a jump back, no sweep). Ping Pong: the direction alternates each leg.
How many legs Loop and Ping Pong run (0 = forever). Ping Pong counts each direction, so 2 = there and back. Ignored in Once mode.
The [Path2D] to follow. It must be in the tree with a non-empty curve; otherwise the spawner stays where it is and a warning prints once.

Optional [Curve] mapping leg time (x, 0..1) to path progress (y). Overrides [member movement_transition] and [member movement_ease]. Progress outside 0..1 is clamped to the path ends; non-finite samples fall back to linear.
Rotate the spawner to face its direction of travel (it turns around on reverse legs).
Extra rotation in degrees on top of the path-facing rotation (for example 90 when the art points up).
Attach: the spawner sits on the path itself (like [PathFollow2D]). Relative To Start: the path's shape is replayed from where the spawner starts, so a path drawn anywhere works as a motion template.
Pixels per second when [member movement_timing] is Speed (each leg takes path length / speed). Must be finite and greater than 0.
Seconds to wait at the start pose before the first leg moves; applied on every fresh start.
Fraction (0..1) of the first leg already elapsed when a run starts.
Duration: each leg takes [member movement_duration_sec]. Speed: each leg takes path length / [member movement_speed].
[enum Tween.TransitionType] easing each leg (Linear, Sine, Quint, Back, ...), identical to a Tween. Hidden when [member movement_progress_curve] is set.
Multiplier on the inherited movement velocity (1 = full momentum, 0.5 = half, negative = backwards).

Orbit direction. DontMove means escort: bullets hold a fixed slot on the ring and follow the target without circling. OrbitRandom rolls OrbitLeft or OrbitRight per bullet when the volley spawns (never DontMove); live volleys keep their rolled direction on retarget passes, so switching to OrbitRandom mid-flight only affects new volleys.

Bullets ring their homing target once they arrive. Needs [member homing_enabled]: orbiting without homing does nothing (volleys fly straight; one warning per configuration, and the setup warnings list it). A freed mid-flight target never crashes: dead entries trim out of the queue, non-finite frames hold the bullet still for one tick, and the lock follows [member orbiting_lock_policy].

Deadzone radius in pixels, used only when [member orbiting_follow_mode] is FollowDeadzone. The ring center stays pinned while the target moves within this distance of the lock point, then re-pins to the target.

How the locked ring follows a moving target. FollowTarget tracks the target 1:1. FollowDeadzone pins the ring center until the target walks farther than [member orbiting_follow_deadzone] from it, absorbing jitter. Anchored freezes the ring where it locked and ignores target motion entirely.

What drops the orbit lock. RelockAlways re-acquires the radius on every retarget. StayLocked never unlocks on retarget or empty queues: once locked, bullets keep their angle and center until you explicitly disable orbiting, clear targets, or the target is freed. RelockOnTargetChange unlocks only when the front target is a different target than the one the bullet locked onto, so the same moving Node2D never breaks the ring. A freed target trims out of the queue instead of crashing: RelockAlways and RelockOnTargetChange fly toward the next live target, StayLocked rides out the gap and re-pins silently when a target returns. For a bodyguard ring on a moving Node2D use StayLocked with FollowTarget (or FollowDeadzone) and a stationary retarget mode.
Orbit ring radius in pixels. Must be at least 0.01.
Fans the radius out per bullet: bullet i orbits with start + step times i (concentric shells).
Orbit radius of the first bullet in linear mode.
Orbit radius growth per bullet in linear mode. May be negative, results clamp at 0.01.

When on, locked OrbitLeft/OrbitRight bullets translate 1:1 with the target and keep circling, exactly like DontMove escorts. When off, locked bullets chase the ring clamped to speed times delta and trail behind fast targets.
How bullet textures face while physically orbiting.

What happens to this spawner's live volleys when the spawner is freed (an enemy dying with its turret, a scene change). Reparenting never triggers it. - [constant ORPHANED_VOLLEYS_KEEP_FLYING] (default): the bullets fly on, but their hits reach nobody: signal connections live on the emitter, so every connection on the freed spawner is gone, even ones whose callback is on a long-lived node. The first unhandled hit prints one warning explaining this. - [constant ORPHANED_VOLLEYS_HAND_TO_FACTORY]: the volleys become factory-owned, so [signal BulletFactory2D.area_entered] and the other factory signals report their hits. The only way an orphan's hits can still be handled. - [constant ORPHANED_VOLLEYS_CLEAR]: every live bullet is cleared with its On Clear effects (a wave that vanishes with its source). - [constant ORPHANED_VOLLEYS_REMOVE]: every live bullet disappears silently and its volley returns to the pool. To keep hit handlers working while the spawner lives, connect to the spawner's signals from a node that outlives it, or set [member BulletVolleyData2D.emit_collision_signals] to [code]false[/code] for bullets that intentionally report nothing.

Auto (default): pattern transforms are generated once and re-posed per shot whenever the pattern provably follows the generator (rigidly, or by translation only); any pattern-affecting property change rebakes automatically. Sources that read outside state (From Children, Aimed, Corridor, Custom, Path2D) and unseeded random patterns always regenerate. A moving or spinning spawner never needs Off. Off: regenerate every shot, for debugging or for scripts that change pattern inputs behind the setters' back.

Scales the whole pattern around the generator (positions and bullet size grow together). 1.0 keeps it as is, 0 collapses it onto the generator, negatives mirror it. Compose with transforms_scale for big-layout + big-bullet looks.

Where volley transforms come from: children markers (0), this generator itself (1), or one of 31 procedural helper patterns (2-32: Grid, Ring, Fan, Spiral, Line, Aimed, Flower, Ellipse, Rain, Scatter, Star Polygon, Multi Spiral, Cross, Star, Heart, Wave, Waterfall, Lattice, Rose, Counter Spiral, Corridor, Lissajous, Custom, Circle, Rectangle, Square, Polygon, Path2D, Triangle, Trapezoid, Diamond). Only the active pattern's options show in the inspector. Every helper draws exactly [member helper_bullets_amount] bullets at distinct spots. Pipeline per volley: generate (with outline placement, fill or layers for the loop shapes), then spin, then pattern/local scale, then helper_skip_indices (so skip indexes match the preview).
Preview arrow color.
Gap in pixels between dot edge and arrow tail.
Preview arrow head length in pixels.
Preview arrow head width in pixels.
Preview arrow length in pixels (multiplied by pattern_scale and transforms_scale, so glyphs stay proportional to the layout).
Preview arrow shaft width in pixels.
Collision-ring overlay color.
Collision-ring overlay line width in pixels.
Preview dot color.
Preview dot radius in pixels (multiplied by pattern_scale and transforms_scale, so glyphs stay proportional to the layout).

When true and spawn_data carries a valid collision shape, the dots layer also draws one outline circle per dot with the shape's bounding radius (circle r, rect min/2, capsule height/2). Compare hitbox vs visual directly in the editor.
Emphasis color for bullet 0 in the preview (pattern start: anchor, reverse, loop seam). Drawn bigger on top of the regular dot.

Extra outline-layer ring color (Layers placement only): one yellow closed ring per ring beyond the base outline, drawn under the dots with the same width as the base track and never antialiased. Same alpha as the base track by default. Empty unless layers are active (count above 1 with valid spacing).

Track underlay color: the shape/loop/curve bullets ride on, drawn as segments under the dots so sparse volleys still show the whole track. Distinct from dots, arrows and the first-bullet marker by default.
Track underlay line width in pixels (multiplied by nothing: absolute screen-ish size). 0 hides the track. Must be finite and 0 or more.

Reload jitter in seconds: each auto volley waits shoot_interval_sec +/- uniform jitter (seeded by [member reload_jitter_seed], floored at 0.001s so fast intervals keep working with jitter on). 0 is exact. Must be finite and 0 or more.

Seed for [member reload_jitter_sec] only. 0 is non-deterministic, otherwise the jitter sequence reproduces exactly; different seeds give independent sequences. Does nothing while [member reload_jitter_sec] is 0. Does not affect any bullet pattern or homing pick.
Delay before the first automatic volley. Applied when the spawner becomes ready and by [method reset_shooting]. Must be finite and 0 or more.

Seconds between automatic volleys. Must be above zero. Shortening it also shortens the wait already running. Runs on an accumulator: overshoot carries over so the average rate is exact at any value (fast intervals repay every due volley in the same tick, up to 8 pulls; hitch backlogs beyond that resync instead of bursting).
Master switch for automatic shooting. [method shoot_once] works regardless.
Shows one dot and facing arrow per bullet in the editor. Follows the generator live. Never saved to the scene.
Also shows the preview while the game runs. Off by default.

Bullet data for each volley. Duplicated once per resource (the spawner keeps the copy until the resource changes or is replaced), so sharing one resource is safe. Assigning the same resource again keeps the copy.

Flat global offset added to every bullet right after spawn (muzzle offsets, spawn-then-nudge). Zero disables the pass. Applied through the engine teleport path, so shapes, attachments, and interpolation stay in sync. Must be finite.

How [member spawn_position_offset] applies. Global (default, the historical behaviour): a world-space shift for every volley. Local: a muzzle offset in the generator's frame, so it turns and scales with the spawner. The preview draws the offset where bullets actually spawn, in both spaces.
How far the pattern swings each way in oscillate mode.
Rotates each volley around the generator at runtime. Editor preview stays still.
Swings per second in oscillate mode.
0 rotates forever, 1 swings back and forth (see amplitude and frequency).
Spin speed in continuous mode. Positive is clockwise.
Warn before firing: emits volley_telegraphed with the current aim, then fires after telegraph_sec. Transforms re-collect at fire time.
Warning time before the volley fires. Must be finite and 0 or more.

Node patterns are built on. Empty means this spawner. Point it at another Node2D to move children markers, helper shapes, spin pivot, scale center, and the preview there. Inside the tree, a path to a non-Node2D is rejected (old value kept).

Per-bullet size scale: multiplies each spawn transform's local basis (texture size) without moving its position. 1.0 keeps sizes as generated, 0 hides bullets in place, negatives mirror them. Must be finite.

signal.name: area_entered
signal.description: Fired live when one of this spawner's bullets enters an area; same contract as [signal BulletFactory2D.area_entered] (the factory stays silent for spawner volleys). Connections live on the spawner: if it is freed they are gone, see [member orphaned_volleys].

signal.name: body_entered
signal.description: Fired live when one of this spawner's bullets hits a body; same contract as [signal BulletFactory2D.body_entered].

signal.name: bounce_area_entered
signal.description: Fired when one of this spawner's bullets bounces off an area. A consumed bounce fires both this and [signal area_entered].

signal.name: bounce_body_entered
signal.description: Fired when one of this spawner's bullets bounces off a body. A consumed bounce fires both this and [signal body_entered].

signal.name: bullet_graze_exited
signal.description: Fired when one of this spawner's bullets leaves a graze zone alive after grazing it. Same payload and contract as [signal BulletFactory2D.bullet_graze_exited], which fires right after this one.

signal.name: bullet_grazed
signal.description: Fired live when one of this spawner's bullets grazes a ring of a zone (see [BulletGrazeZone2D]). Same payload and contract as [signal BulletFactory2D.bullet_grazed], which fires right after this one for the same graze: count graze on one of the two. Once this spawner is freed its flying bullets keep grazing and only the factory signal fires.

signal.name: burst_finished
signal.description: Fired once whenever a burst chain ends: after its last shot, when it aborts after a full burst's worth of consecutive failed shots (a failed shot is retried, never silently consumed; each attempt reports through volley_skipped), or when it is cancelled (auto-fire or burst mode switched off, burst_count shrunk below the shots already fired).

signal.name: burst_shot_fired
signal.description: Fired for every shot inside a burst chain, with the 1-based shot number and whether this shot fired mirrored. The mirror rhythm always starts plain: plain, mirrored, plain, ... for any burst_count.

signal.name: homing_targets_resolved
signal.description: Fired once per homing volley with the resolved targets (Node2D or Vector2 entries), before [signal volley_homing_configured]. Empty for the Mouse source and for volleys that found nothing. Not fired while homing is off. A handler may queue_free the volley: the shot is then dropped (volley_skipped "dropped").

signal.name: life_time_over
signal.description: Fired live when this spawner's bullets expire (needs the lifetime signal enabled in the spawn data); same contract as [signal BulletFactory2D.life_time_over]: the listed bullets are alive in the handler and die right after it unless their life was extended.

signal.name: movement_endpoint_reached
signal.description: Emitted each time a leg reaches its endpoint. [param at_end] is true at the path end, false at the path start. Fires before [signal movement_loop_completed] or [signal movement_finished] for the same leg.

signal.name: movement_finished
signal.description: Emitted once when a finite run completes (Once mode, or after [member movement_loops] legs). Not emitted by [method movement_stop].

signal.name: movement_loop_completed
signal.description: Emitted after each completed leg that is not the last one (Loop and Ping Pong). [param leg_index] is the 0-based index of the leg that just finished.

signal.name: movement_started
signal.description: Emitted when the movement starts or resumes playing ([method movement_play] or autostart).

signal.name: pattern_list_finished
signal.description: Fired once when a pattern list completes, in both modes (sequential: after the last entry fires; simultaneous: after all entries fired).

signal.name: pre_shoot
signal.description: Last-chance hook fired after the volley has spawned and been stamped, but before homing/orbiting is configured and before volley_fired. Handlers may tweak the live volley through its API (speed ramp, difficulty scale); the spawn data has already been consumed at this point. Same handler contract as volley_fired: never call shoot_once from here (use shoot_once_deferred).

signal.name: retarget_applied
signal.description: Fired after an automatic interval retarget pass that touched at least one volley. HUD and wave logic can observe tracking health from this.

signal.name: shooting_finished
signal.description: Fired when the volley counter reaches [member max_volleys] while auto-shooting is enabled. Manual shots on a spawner with [member shooting_enabled] off never report it.

signal.name: shooting_started
signal.description: Fired when automatic shooting turns on.

signal.name: shooting_stopped
signal.description: Fired when automatic shooting turns off via [member shooting_enabled].

signal.name: volley_bullet_homing_target_reached
signal.description: Fired live when a bullet of one of this spawner's volleys reaches its homing target (also emitted on the volley as [signal BulletVolley2D.bullet_homing_target_reached]). Target is null for position and mouse targets. Connect here rather than on volley instances: a volley drops its own connections when it returns to the pool.

signal.name: volley_fired
signal.description: Fired for every volley, with a 1-based counter.

signal.name: volley_homing_configured
signal.description: Fired for every homing/orbiting volley right after it is configured, before [signal volley_fired]. Only fires when homing or orbiting is enabled.

signal.name: volley_skipped
signal.description: Fired whenever a shot does not produce a volley, with the reason: "no_factory", "no_spawn_data", "no_transforms" (empty pattern), "over_budget" (max_live_bullets), "outside_fire_arc" (homing fire arc), "factory_refused" (the factory rejected the spawn) or "dropped" (a handler freed or took over the volley before it was configured). Games can fall back on these instead of reading the log.

signal.name: volley_telegraphed
signal.description: Fired when a telegraph warning starts, with a snapshot of the current aim (advisory: the actual fire re-collects transforms). Draw warning lines, flash markers, play the cue.
